title: Western Sahara's lost mission, hacked alert apps and F1's youngest champion

stories.headline: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after Russian veto
stories.headlineZh: 俄罗斯否决后，联合国西撒哈拉维和任务终止
stories.summaryZh: 安理会未能续签授权，运行约35年的西撒特派团结束，古特雷斯警告冲突升级风险。
stories.c1:
A United Nations peacekeeping mission that has watched over Western Sahara for roughly 35 years has officially come to an end, after the Security Council failed to agree on renewing its mandate. The mission, known as MINURSO, was set up in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum on the territory's future. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres confirmed on Sunday that it had entered a liquidation phase, with its equipment being returned to the countries that had contributed troops.

The deadlock stems from a long-running dispute. Morocco has controlled the desert territory, which is roughly the size of Britain, since Spain withdrew in 1975, while the Algeria-backed Polisario Front is seeking an independent Sahrawi state. A US-drafted resolution would have extended the mission for a year but made Morocco's autonomy plan the sole basis for future negotiations. Although 11 of the 15 council members backed it, Russia used its veto, and a rival Russian draft was subsequently voted down.

Predictably, reactions split along familiar lines. Morocco's royal palace welcomed the outcome as a significant development, whereas Algeria expressed deep regret and accused Washington of excessive bias towards Rabat. The US ambassador, Mike Waltz, described the veto as unfortunate and argued that the status quo was unacceptable, while his Russian counterpart, Vassily Nebenzia, insisted that the council could not predetermine questions of sovereignty.

For now, the most pressing concern is security on the ground. Guterres said he remained worried about the risk of hostilities escalating and urged all sides "to exercise maximum restraint". Without international monitors in place, it may well become harder to keep track of developments in the territory. Whether diplomacy can fill the gap left by the mission, however, remains an open question.
stories.b2:
A United Nations peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has ended after about 35 years. The UN Security Council could not agree to renew it. The mission, called MINURSO, started in 1991. Its job was to watch over a ceasefire and prepare a vote on the territory's future. On Sunday, UN chief Antonio Guterres confirmed that its equipment was being sent back to the countries that provided troops.

The problem is an old dispute. Morocco has controlled the desert territory since Spain left in 1975. The Polisario Front, which is supported by Algeria, wants an independent state. The United States wrote a plan that would have kept the mission going for another year. Eleven of the 15 council members supported it, but Russia used its veto. A different Russian plan was also rejected.

Morocco welcomed the result, while Algeria said it deeply regretted it and accused the US of favouring Morocco. The US ambassador said the situation could not stay the same. Russia's ambassador said the council should not decide who owns the territory.

Guterres said he was worried that fighting could get worse, and he asked all sides to stay calm. Without UN monitors, it may be harder to know what is happening there.

vocab.example: The panel insisted it would not predetermine the outcome of the review.

questions.q: MINURSO was originally created to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a vote on the territory's future.
questions.explain: 文中说 "set up in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum"，与题干一致。

questions.q: Most Security Council members opposed the US-drafted resolution.
questions.explain: 文中说 "11 of the 15 council members backed it"，多数成员支持，因此题干错误。

questions.q: Algeria plans to send its own troops into the territory to replace the UN monitors.
questions.explain: 文中只提到阿尔及利亚表示 "deep regret"，并未提到派兵计划。

questions.q: Why did the US-drafted resolution fail?
options: Fewer than half of the council members supported it.
Russia used its veto against it.
The Polisario Front asked for it to be withdrawn.
questions.explain: 文中说 "Russia used its veto"，尽管多数成员支持，否决权使决议未能通过。

stories.discuss: Why do you think international peacekeeping missions sometimes last for decades without solving the underlying conflict? Should there be a time limit on them?

stories.headline: Australia's first Indigenous-owned water testing lab opens in Bundaberg
stories.headlineZh: 澳大利亚首个原住民所有的水质检测实验室在班达伯格开业
stories.summaryZh: 昆士兰原住民机构开设水质实验室，样本不再送往布里斯班，也为原住民从事科学铺路。
stories.c1:
An Aboriginal organisation in central Queensland has opened what is believed to be Australia's first Indigenous-owned water testing laboratory, a milestone that its founders hope will put scientific authority firmly in the hands of traditional owners. Built by the Gidarjil Development Corporation beside the Burnett River at Bundaberg Port, the lab is called Nyamgim Gung, which means "looking at water" in the Gurang language.

Until now, samples collected on country had to be sent to Brisbane, about 400 kilometres away, for analysis, which inevitably slowed things down. The new facility specialises in seawater but can also test river, fresh and brackish water, measuring nutrients, trace elements, hardness and alkalinity with the help of advanced automation. Lab manager Nirali Vadgama, an environmental scientist, has been working towards this moment since 2022, and in September the lab gained national and international accreditation.

Beyond speeding up results, the project is fundamentally about self-determination. The lab was established on behalf of four traditional owner groups, and Gidarjil, a not-for-profit, can generate income by selling its testing services to other organisations. Chief executive Margaret Blackman has presented the venture as an example of thinking outside the box, and the corporation hopes to help other Aboriginal groups along the coast manage their own land and sea country.

There is also a long-term ambition: to attract more Indigenous people into scientific careers and, eventually, to have the lab run entirely by Indigenous staff. Alongside the opening, Gidarjil launched Dulba Muni, its first all-female ranger program, whose members help to collect and prepare samples. Admittedly, a single lab cannot transform regional science overnight, but it does suggest that high-level research need not be confined to big cities.
stories.b2:
An Aboriginal organisation in Queensland has opened what is believed to be Australia's first Indigenous-owned water testing lab. The Gidarjil Development Corporation built it next to the Burnett River at Bundaberg Port. Its name, Nyamgim Gung, means "looking at water" in the Gurang language.

In the past, water samples had to be sent to Brisbane, about 400 kilometres away, so results took longer. The new lab mainly tests seawater, but it can also test river water and fresh water. It uses modern automated equipment. The lab manager, environmental scientist Nirali Vadgama, has worked on the project since 2022. In September, the lab received national and international accreditation.

The lab is also about giving traditional owners more control. It was built for four traditional owner groups. Gidarjil is a not-for-profit, and it can earn money by selling testing services to other organisations. It also wants to help other Aboriginal groups on the coast look after their land and sea.

In the long term, Gidarjil hopes more Indigenous people will choose careers in science, and that one day the lab will be run only by Indigenous staff. It has also started its first all-female ranger program.

vocab.example: Finishing her first marathon was a real milestone for her.

Having the lab run entirely by Indigenous staff

stories.discuss: Why do you think it matters who owns and runs scientific facilities in a community? Could this model spread to other areas of research?

stories.headline: Hackers send false nuclear warnings through Ukraine's air raid app
stories.headlineZh: 黑客通过乌克兰防空警报应用发送虚假核威胁警告
stories.summaryZh: 乌克兰防空警报应用遭入侵发出假核化警报，俄罗斯应急应用随后也称遭大规模网络攻击。
stories.c1:
Ukraine's official air raid alert app was hacked on Sunday evening, briefly bombarding users with false warnings that Kyiv and surrounding areas faced nuclear and chemical threats, and even possible street fighting. One bogus message claimed that Russia had launched its Oreshnik hypersonic missile. The Ukrainian Air Force moved quickly to reassure the public, telling people there was no radiation threat and urging them to stay calm and rely on its official channel.

Hours later, Russia's Emergencies Ministry reported that its own warning app, which alerts people to incoming drone attacks, had been hit by what it called a massive cyberattack spreading false information. Ukraine's Centre for Strategic Communications pointed the finger at Moscow, citing Russian-language text in one of the fake alerts, whereas the Russian ministry did not say whom it held responsible. It remains unclear whether the two incidents were connected.

The timing was striking: the hack came just as a localised truce in the Russian-occupied part of the Kherson region ended. That pause, described as the longest of the war so far, had allowed hundreds of stranded residents to leave the town of Oleshky. Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks on Kherson resumed on Monday.

Although sirens and other alert channels kept working throughout, the episode exposes a worrying vulnerability. In a country where people may have only minutes to find shelter from a ballistic missile, an app that cries wolf could erode public trust in warnings that are genuinely life-saving. It also serves as a reminder that, in modern conflicts, digital infrastructure has become very much part of the battlefield.
stories.b2:
Ukraine's official air raid alert app was hacked on Sunday evening. For a short time, it sent false warnings that Kyiv and nearby areas faced nuclear and chemical threats. One fake message said Russia had fired a hypersonic missile. The Ukrainian Air Force quickly told people there was no radiation threat and asked them to stay calm.

A few hours later, Russia said its own emergency app, which warns people about drone attacks, had also suffered a big cyberattack. A Ukrainian government centre blamed Russia, because one fake message was written in Russian. Russia did not say who it blamed. Nobody knows yet if the two attacks were connected.

The hack happened just as a local ceasefire in part of the Kherson region ended. This ceasefire was described as the longest of the war so far. It allowed hundreds of people who were stuck in the town of Oleshky to leave. Ukraine said Russia started attacking Kherson again on Monday.

Sirens and other warning systems kept working. However, the attack shows a serious weakness. People sometimes have only minutes to find shelter, so false alarms could make them trust real warnings less.

vocab.zh: 连续轰炸；（信息）狂轰滥炸
vocab.en: to direct a large amount of something at someone
vocab.example: Since I signed up, the shop has been bombarding me with emails.

questions.explain: 文中说俄方 "did not say whom it held responsible"，并未指责乌克兰，因此题干错误。

questions.q: One of the fake messages said Russia had launched a hypersonic missile.
questions.explain: 文中说 "One bogus message claimed that Russia had launched its Oreshnik hypersonic missile"。

questions.explain: 文中没有提到黑客索要钱财，属于未提及。

questions.q: What happened around the time the Ukrainian app was hacked?
options: A local truce in the Kherson region ended.
Kyiv launched a new city alert app.
Air raid sirens across Ukraine stopped working.
Russia agreed to extend the ceasefire.
questions.explain: 文中说 "the hack came just as a localised truce ... ended"；而警报器一直正常 ("sirens ... kept working")。

stories.discuss: Why do you think governments rely more and more on apps to warn citizens about danger? What are the risks, and how could they be reduced?

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli, 20, becomes Formula 1's youngest ever champion
stories.headlineZh: 20岁的安东内利成为史上最年轻F1世界冠军
stories.summaryZh: 梅赛德斯车手安东内利在墨西哥城大奖赛获第三，提前四站锁定总冠军并打破维特尔纪录。
stories.c1:
Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, sealing the title at the Mexico City Grand Prix at just 20 years and 68 days old. The Mercedes driver needed only to finish ninth or better, and he did considerably more than that, starting fourth and overtaking Charles Leclerc late in the race to take third place. "It's a day I will remember forever," he said afterwards.

His triumph rewrites the record books. The previous youngest champion, Sebastian Vettel, was 23 years and 134 days old when he won in 2010, so Antonelli has broken the record by a remarkable margin. He is also the first Italian to claim the drivers' title since Alberto Ascari in 1953, ending a wait of more than seven decades for one of the sport's most passionate fan bases.

The race itself was far from straightforward. Max Verstappen, who started fifth, came through to win, with Lewis Hamilton second. The race was red-flagged on lap 44 of 71 when a wheel came off Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac under braking and he hit the wall, although he was able to walk away. Australia's Oscar Piastri, meanwhile, started 12th and finished seventh after a collision with Arvid Lindblad left his car damaged.

With four rounds still remaining, the championship was wrapped up unusually early, which arguably underlines how dominant Antonelli's season has been. His success will inevitably prompt debate about how quickly young drivers should be promoted to top teams. Still, few would dispute that, for someone of his age, he has handled intense pressure with impressive composure.
stories.b2:
Kimi Antonelli is now the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. The Mercedes driver won the title at the Mexico City Grand Prix when he was 20 years and 68 days old. He only needed to finish ninth, but he started fourth and passed Charles Leclerc near the end to finish third.

The record had belonged to Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 when he won in 2010. Antonelli is also the first Italian driver to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Italian fans had waited more than 70 years for this moment.

The race was exciting. Max Verstappen started fifth and won it, and Lewis Hamilton came second. The race was stopped on lap 44 after a wheel came off Valtteri Bottas's car and he hit the wall. Luckily, he was able to walk away. Australian driver Oscar Piastri started 12th and finished seventh after a crash with another car damaged his.

There are still four races left in the season, so Antonelli won the title very early. This shows how strong his season has been. Some people may now ask whether young drivers should join top teams so quickly, but most agree he has dealt with the pressure very well.

vocab.en: to make a championship win certain
vocab.example: A late goal helped the club seal the title with two games to spare.

vocab.en: to set new records
vocab.example: The young swimmer rewrote the record books at the national championships.

vocab.en: by a surprisingly large amount
vocab.example: The new model outsold its rivals by a remarkable margin.

vocab.en: quite complicated or difficult
vocab.example: Getting a visa turned out to be far from straightforward.

vocab.en: to escape from an accident without serious injury
vocab.example: Both drivers were lucky to walk away from the crash.

vocab.en: to finish or complete something
vocab.example: Let's wrap up the meeting by five so everyone can catch their train.

vocab.en: to show clearly that something is important or true
vocab.example: The survey underlines the need for cheaper childcare.

vocab.en: to cause people to discuss or argue about something
vocab.example: The decision to close the pool has prompted debate in the community.

vocab.en: the state of being calm and in control
vocab.example: She kept her composure even when the questions became hostile.

questions.q: Antonelli won the Mexico City Grand Prix.
questions.explain: 文中说 Verstappen "came through to win"，而 Antonelli 获得 "third place"，因此题干错误。

questions.q: Sebastian Vettel was over 23 years old when he became champion in 2010.
questions.explain: 文中说 Vettel "was 23 years and 134 days old when he won in 2010"，即超过23岁。

questions.q: Antonelli has signed a new contract to stay with Mercedes next season.
questions.explain: 文中没有提到他的合同情况，属于未提及。

questions.q: Why was the race stopped with a red flag?
options: Heavy rain made the track unsafe.
A wheel came off Bottas's car and he hit the wall.
questions.explain: 文中说 "red-flagged on lap 44 of 71 when a wheel came off Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac"。

stories.discuss: Why do you think some athletes reach the top of their sport at a very young age? Is early success always a good thing for them?

dialogue.title: Stuck at Flinders Street
dialogue.setting: On a weekday evening, two former uni classmates bump into each other on a crowded platform at Flinders Street Station while their train is delayed.
dialogue.settingZh: 工作日傍晚，两位大学老同学在弗林德斯街站拥挤的站台上偶遇，他们的列车正在延误。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Hang on, is that you, Tom? I haven't seen you since graduation!
lines.zh: 等等，是你吗，汤姆？毕业以后就没见过你了！

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Priya! Small world. Don't tell me you're on the Sandringham line too?
lines.zh: 普丽娅！世界真小。别告诉我你也坐桑德灵厄姆线？

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Afraid so. The board says twenty minutes, but I'll believe it when I see it.
lines.zh: 恐怕是的。显示屏说二十分钟，但我得亲眼看到才信。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Apparently there's a signal fault near Richmond. Same old story, really.
lines.zh: 听说里士满附近信号出了故障。老问题了，真的。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Typical. I was hoping to get home early and actually cook for once.
lines.zh: 真是一贯如此。我本来想早点回家，难得自己做顿饭。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Ha, I'd pencilled in a run, but that's probably out the window now.
lines.zh: 哈，我原本打算去跑步，现在估计泡汤了。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: So what are you up to these days? Still doing the data stuff?
lines.zh: 那你最近在忙什么？还在做数据那一块吗？

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Sort of. I've moved into cyber security, which keeps me on my toes.
lines.zh: 算是吧。我转做网络安全了，让我时刻保持警惕。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Oh, you must've seen that story about the hacked air raid app, then.
lines.zh: 哦，那你肯定看到那条防空警报应用被黑的新闻了。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Yeah, it's a nightmare scenario. If people stop trusting alerts, you're in real trouble.
lines.zh: 是啊，这是最糟糕的情况。如果人们不再相信警报，那就真麻烦了。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Makes you wonder how secure our own systems are, doesn't it?
lines.zh: 让人不禁想，我们自己的系统有多安全，对吧？

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Don't get me started. Anyway, it looks like our train's finally pulling in.
lines.zh: 别让我开始说这个。总之，看起来我们的车终于进站了。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Thank goodness. Let's grab a coffee properly some time and catch up.
lines.zh: 谢天谢地。改天好好喝杯咖啡叙叙旧吧。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Definitely. I'll message you this week, and I mean it this time!
lines.zh: 一定。我这周就给你发消息，这次是认真的！

phrases.plain: What a coincidence to meet you here!
phrases.zh: 偶遇熟人时的常用感叹

phrases.en: I'll believe it when I see it.
phrases.zh: 表示怀疑，要亲眼见到才信

phrases.en: that's probably out the window now

phrases.plain: I have a lot to say about that.
Let's meet and talk about our news.
phrases.en: Let's grab a coffee properly some time and catch up.
